Here’s a 4-week on-ramp block for your client at 10–13 weeks postpartum. It progresses conservatively, honors the no-jumping restriction for 4 more weeks, and uses home space plus light dumbbells. Emphasis is on breathing mechanics, core and pelvic floor reconditioning, gradually increasing total volume and complexity, and establishing sustainable habits. Week 1 is an acclimatisation week (lower volume/intensity). Assume 3 sessions/week plus optional low-intensity activity. If she has any pelvic floor symptoms (heaviness, doming/coning, leakage, pain), regress immediately and/or reduce load, range, or tempo.

Global guidelines
- Tools: light DBs (2–8 kg each as tolerated), mini-band/long band if available, chair/bench/couch, towel.
- Breathing and core: Exhale on effort, maintain “exhale to exert” and soft brace (deep core + pelvic floor lift on exhale, relax on inhale).
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 seconds down), smooth concentrics. No breath holding.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7/10 on work sets. Leave 2–3 reps in reserve in Weeks 1–2; 1–2 in Weeks 3–4.
- Rest: 45–75 seconds between accessory sets, 75–120 seconds for compound sets.
- Walking: Aim 20–35 minutes most days at conversational pace; can split into 10–15 minute bouts.
- Red flags: Stop/modify if pain >3/10, pressure or bulge sensations, increased bleeding, doming you can’t correct with breath, or incontinence.

Progression overview
- Week 1: Acclimatisation. Low volume, foundational breath, re-introduce patterns (hinge, squat to box, push, pull, carry), short sessions.
- Week 2: Build volume. Add sets/reps; introduce slow-eccentric work; light DB loading on more moves.
- Week 3: Add complexity. Offset/anti-rotation elements, half-kneeling presses/rows, slightly longer circuits.
- Week 4: Pre-transition. Increase density or load, introduce low-impact power (no jumping): step drives, tempo changes.

Core/pelvic floor daily micro-practice (5–8 minutes, daily)
- 3D rib breathing x 5–8 breaths (hands on lower ribs).
- Supine 90/90 heel taps or heel slides x 6–8/side, 1–2 sets. Exhale as heel moves, avoid doming.
- Side-lying or quadruped pelvic floor lifts: 6–8 gentle contractions, 2–3-second lift, 4–6-second release, 1–2 sets. One longer 10–15-second endurance hold.
- Optional: Cat-cow x 6, thread-the-needle x 6/side for thoracic mobility.

WEEK 1 (Acclimatisation)
Format: 3 sessions, ~30–35 minutes. Keep RPE ~5–6.

Session A
- Reset/Breath: Crocodile or 3D rib breathing 5 breaths; 90/90 with banded pull-apart (light band) x 8
- Prep: Quadruped rock back to bear hover (no lift yet) x 6; Dead bug arms only x 6/side
- Strength Circuit x 2 rounds
  1) Sit-to-box squat bodyweight, arms forward reach: 8–10
  2) Elevated hip hinge to chair (hands on thighs for feedback): 8–10
  3) Incline push-up on counter/wall: 6–8
  4) Half-kneeling single-arm band row or light DB row (support front knee down): 8/side
  5) Standing suitcase carry light DB: 20–30 meters/side (or 20–30 seconds)
- Finisher (optional): Marching bridge (slow) x 6/side; Standing calf raises x 10

Session B
- Reset: Seated breathing with reach x 5 breaths
- Prep: Side-lying open book x 6/side; Glute bridge with 3-second exhale x 8
- Strength Circuit x 2 rounds
  1) Goblet box squat light DB: 8
  2) DB RDL light pair: 8
  3) Half-kneeling overhead landmine press pattern using single DB press path (press slightly forward/up): 6–8/side (use very light)
  4) Tall-kneeling band pulldown or supported DB row: 8–10
  5) Pallof press (band) or anti-rotation hold: 10-second hold x 3/side
- Finisher: Farmer carry light pair x 30–45 seconds

Session C
- Reset: 90/90 heel taps x 6/side
- Prep: World’s greatest stretch (short) x 3/side; Ankle rocks x 10
- Strength Circuit x 2 rounds
  1) Step-back supported split squat to chair tap (hands on counter): 6/side
  2) Hip hinge to DB RDL: 8
  3) Incline chest press on floor (floor press) light DBs: 8–10
  4) Quadruped row (bird dog row with light DB or band) x 6–8/side
  5) Tall-kneeling anti-extension band pulldown (press-down) x 8–10
- Finisher: Dead bug heel taps x 6/side slow

Low-intensity options this week: 2–3 easy walks, 1 mobility day (10–15 minutes).

WEEK 2 (Build volume)
Format: 3 sessions, ~35–40 minutes. Add a set to main circuits (3 rounds). Slightly increase DB load or reps. RPE ~6–7.

Session A
- Reset/Prep: 90/90 breathing with band pull-apart x 8; Quadruped hover (knees float 1 inch) 3 x 10 seconds
- Strength Circuit x 3 rounds
  1) Goblet squat to box (or remove box if mechanics hold): 8–10
  2) DB RDL pair: 8–10 with 3-second eccentric
  3) Incline push-up on counter: 8–10
  4) Half-kneeling single-arm row: 8–10/side
  5) Suitcase carry moderate DB: 30–40 seconds/side
- Accessory Core
  - Side plank from knees 2 x 15–20 seconds/side
  - Heel slides 2 x 8/side

Session B
- Reset/Prep: Glute bridge with 5-second exhale x 8; T-spine rotation x 6/side
- Strength Circuit x 3 rounds
  1) Split squat supported (light fingertip support): 6–8/side
  2) Hip hinge to wall touch (drill) then DB RDL: 8–10
  3) Half-kneeling single-arm overhead press light: 6–8/side (stop before rib flare)
  4) Band pulldown or 1-arm DB row bench-supported: 8–10/side
  5) Pallof press: 8 reps with 2–3-second hold each,/side
- Finisher: Marching bridge 2 x 8/side

Session C
- Reset/Prep: Cat-cow x 6; Bear position shoulder taps from elevated surface 2 x 8/side
- Strength Circuit x 3 rounds
  1) Box squat or air squat tempo 3-1-1: 8
  2) Hip bridge feet elevated on step: 8–10
  3) Floor press light–moderate DBs: 8–10
  4) 1/2-kneeling lat-focused row (elbow path low to ribs): 8–10/side
  5) Anti-extension dead-bug press (press DB up as you extend heel) 6–8/side
- Conditioning (low impact): 8–10 minutes continuous easy flow: 1 minute brisk walk + 30 seconds farmer carry + 30 seconds bodyweight good mornings; repeat, nasal breathing if possible.

WEEK 3 (Complexity and anti-rotation)
Format: 3 sessions, ~40–45 minutes. Keep technique first; introduce offset loading and unilateral demands. RPE ~6–7.

Session A
- Reset/Prep: 90/90 lift with exhale x 6; Quadruped hover 3 x 12–15 seconds
- Strength Tri-Set x 3 rounds
  1) Offset goblet squat (hold single DB at chest, slightly off-center) 8–10/side
  2) DB RDL with 2–3-second eccentric 8–10
  3) Elevated push-up lower angle than before (bench vs counter) 8–10
- Accessory x 2 rounds
  4) 1-arm DB row, bench-supported 10–12/side
  5) Standing Pallof press to overhead raise (press out, then raise to forehead height) 6–8/side
  6) Suitcase carry moderate DB 40–50 seconds/side

Session B
- Reset/Prep: Glute bridge with band around knees (if available) x 10; Half-kneeling hip flexor + posterior tilt x 30 seconds/side
- Strength Circuit x 3 rounds
  1) Supported split squat to full range as tolerated 8–10/side
  2) Hip hinge progression: kickstand RDL (rear toe light) 8–10/side
  3) Half-kneeling single-arm overhead press 8–10/side
  4) Tall-kneeling band pulldown 10–12
  5) Side plank (knees) 20–25 seconds/side
- Finisher: Marching bridge 2 x 10/side slow; Standing calf raises 12–15

Session C
- Reset/Prep: Bear position shoulder taps from floor or low elevation 2 x 8/side; T-spine rotations x 6/side
- Strength Supersets x 3 rounds
  A1) Tempo squat 3-1-1 8–10
  A2) Floor press with alternating press (1 arm at a time) 8/side
  B1) DB RDL 10
  B2) Bird-dog row (light) 8/side
- Core/Carry
  - Anti-rotation hold: Pallof iso 15–20 seconds x 2/side
  - Front rack carry with single DB (unilateral) 25–35 seconds/side
- Conditioning (low impact power emphasis without jumping): 2–3 sets
  - Step-up knee drive (slow, control ribcage; use low step) 6–8/side
  - Speed skater pattern without hop (lateral step and reach) 6–8/side
  - Rest as needed, keep breath controlled

WEEK 4 (Pre-transition and density)
Format: 3 sessions, ~40–45 minutes. Slight bump in density or load; maintain symptom-free execution. Still no jumping. RPE ~6.5–7.5.

Session A
- Reset/Prep: 90/90 breathing x 5; Quadruped hover with slow marches 2 x 6/side
- Strength Circuit x 3–4 rounds (choose density: keep rest modest)
  1) Goblet squat (no box if form solid) 8–10
  2) Kickstand RDL 8–10/side
  3) Elevated push-up at lowest manageable height 8–12
  4) 1-arm DB row 10–12/side
  5) Suitcase carry or front rack carry 40–60 seconds/side
- Core: Dead bug with banded pulldown or DB press-out 2 x 8/side; Side plank 2 x 20–25 seconds/side

Session B
- Reset/Prep: Glute bridge 2-second iso at top x 8; Hip airplanes supported (hands on chair) x 4/side
- Strength Supersets x 3–4 rounds
  A1) Split squat 8–10/side
  A2) Half-kneeling single-arm overhead press 8–10/side
  B1) DB RDL 10–12
  B2) Tall-kneeling band pulldown 10–12
- Finisher (low-impact power and control): Continuous 8–10 minutes EMOM-style
  - Minute 1: Step-up knee drive x 8/side (control)
  - Minute 2: Farmer carry 45–60 seconds
  - Minute 3: Anti-rotation walkout holds 10–15 seconds x 2/side
  Repeat for 2–3 rounds depending on tolerance.

Session C
- Reset/Prep: Bear shoulder taps 2 x 8/side; Open books x 6/side
- Strength Tri-Set x 3 rounds
  1) Tempo squat 3-1-1 8–10
  2) Floor press alternating 10/side
  3) Kickstand RDL 8–10/side
- Accessory x 2 rounds
  4) Pallof press to overhead raise 8/side
  5) Marching bridge 10/side slow
  6) Standing calf raises 12–15
- Conditioning: Brisk walk 10–12 minutes with nasal breathing focus; log RPE.

Cool-down each session (3–5 minutes)
- Child’s pose with side reach x 3 breaths/side
- 90/90 breathing x 5 breaths
- Gentle adductor rock-backs x 6–8
- Pelvic floor relax: 4–5 slow belly breaths, cue “drop and melt” on inhale.

Monitoring and modifications
- If coning appears: reduce range, exhale earlier, lighten load; swap to more supported variation (e.g., floor press instead of push-up; bridge instead of RDL).
- If pelvic heaviness/leakage: reduce intensity/volume that day; prioritize supine/side-lying core and glute bridges; avoid prolonged carries that increase pressure.
- C-section note (if applicable): Watch scar sensitivity; avoid prolonged prone pressure early, add gentle scar mobilization only if cleared.

Simple nutrition and recovery anchors
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day; extra 500 ml around sessions. If breastfeeding, add ~300–500 kcal/day total intake.
- Protein: Target 20–30 g high-quality protein at 3–4 meals/day to support recovery.
- Carbs: Include a fist-sized portion pre- or post-workout for energy.
- Micronutrients: Iron, choline, DHA, calcium, and vitamin D per medical guidance; continue prenatal/postnatal if prescribed.
- Sleep: Protect a 20–30 minute daytime nap if nights are fragmented; 5–10 minutes of downregulating breath before bed.
- Soreness: Expect mild DOMS only. Use walking, mobility, and gentle stretching; avoid prolonged static stretching of pelvic floor.

At the end of Week 4
- Reassess: RPE trends, symptom log, ability to maintain brace and breathing under load, push-up height progress, split-squat depth, carry duration.
- If symptom-free and OB clears impact after the 4-week window, transition next block to include gentle impact progressions (e.g., pogo holds, low step hops), add load to squats/RDLs, and introduce simple conditioning intervals.

- Duration: Start 15–25 minutes per bout; build to 30–40 minutes by Week 4 if well tolerated.
- Frequency: 2–4 sessions/week, mixed with strength days or added as separate short bouts.
- Posture/breath: Neutral ribcage/pelvis, steady nasal-in-nose/mouth-out breathing when possible; exhale on any harder efforts.
- Pelvic floor screen: Stop/modify if heaviness/pressure, leakage, increased bleeding, or core doming appears. Reduce cadence/resistance, shorten sessions, or switch modality.
- Impact: No running or hopping until cleared. Avoid maximal, out-of-saddle “sprinting” efforts in this block.

Spin/cycling guidance
- Bike fit: Saddle height so knee has slight bend at bottom; handlebar a bit higher than saddle early on to reduce trunk flexion/pressure. Choose a supportive saddle.
- Seated bias: Keep most work seated. Out-of-saddle climbing can be tested in short 10–20-second bouts late in the block if completely symptom-free, but it’s optional.
- Resistance: Moderate, “road under the wheel.” Avoid grinding (>70 rpm with heavy load) or maximal high-cadence spins (>100–110 rpm) early; aim 80–95 rpm steady.
- Interval structure examples
  - Week 1: 15–20 minutes continuous easy–moderate spin (RPE 5–6). Optional: last 5 minutes add 10-second gentle pickups every 1–2 minutes.
  - Week 2: 25–30 minutes. 3–4 x 2 minutes at RPE 6–7 with 2 minutes easy between.
  - Week 3: 28–35 minutes. 6–8 x 60 seconds at RPE ~7 with 90 seconds easy. Stay seated.
  - Week 4: 30–40 minutes. Pyramid: 1–2–3–2–1 minutes at RPE 6.5–7 with equal easy spins; or 3 x 4 minutes steady RPE 6.5 with 2 minutes easy.
- Cool-down: 3–5 minutes easy spin, then 3–5 minutes of downregulating breathing/mobility.

Other low-impact cardio options
- Brisk walking: 20–40 minutes at conversational pace. Add slight hills only if symptom-free; keep stride compact and cadence higher to reduce ground reaction forces.
- Elliptical: 15–30 minutes, moderate resistance, smooth cadence. Great swap if saddle pressure is uncomfortable.
- Low-impact circuits (no jumping), 8–15 minutes after strength or as standalone:
  - 1 minute brisk walk or stepper
  - 30–45 seconds farmer carry (light–moderate)
  - 30–45 seconds bodyweight good mornings
  - 30–45 seconds marching bridge or step-up knee drives (controlled)
  Repeat 3–5 rounds, keeping RPE 6–7 and breathing steady.
- Step-ups: Low step, controlled knee drive, 8–12 minutes continuous alternating sets of 8–12/side with short rests.

How to integrate with the 4-week on-ramp
- Minimum effective dose: 2 spin/walk sessions per week on non-consecutive days.
- If pairing with strength, do cardio after strength or in a separate session later in the day.
- Example weekly layout:
  - Mon: Strength A + optional 10–12 min easy spin cool-down
  - Tue: Spin 20–30 min (as per week progression)
  - Thu: Strength B
  - Fri or Sat: Spin 25–35 min or brisk walk 30–40 min
  - Sun: Mobility + easy 15–20 min walk

Monitoring and progression
- Progress only if symptom-free during and 24 hours after. If pelvic symptoms appear with cycling, reduce resistance, shorten intervals, stay fully seated, or sub elliptical/walk.
- If C-section sensitivity: adjust bike posture to keep trunk more upright; consider elliptical or brisk walking until saddle is comfortable.

Absolutely. Here’s an anti-flexion–focused core add-on you can layer onto the 4-week on-ramp. Emphasis is on resisting spinal flexion while coordinating breath and pelvic floor. No crunches; mostly supine, side-lying, quadruped, kneeling, and carries. Keep all sets symptom-free (no doming, heaviness, leakage, pain).

How to use
- Frequency: 2–3x/week after strength sessions, or as standalone 10–15 minute minis.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7, leave 1–3 reps in reserve. Exhale on effort, soft 360° brace.
- Progression: Add seconds, reps, or a light DB/band before moving to the next week’s variations.

Week 1 (acclimatisation; foundation)
- Dead bug ISO press: 2 sets x 5–6/side, 3–4-second exhale as you press DB or band straight up while opposite heel taps. Pause and hold tension; no rib flare.
- Side plank (knees) with top-leg abduction: 2 x 12–15 seconds/side. Keep hips stacked; small lift of top knee/foot adds anti-flexion and lateral stability.
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension pulldown: 2 x 8–10 controlled reps. Band anchored high; ribs down, glutes lightly on.
- Suitcase carry (light): 2 x 20–30 seconds/side, walk tall without leaning.

Week 2 (volume and time-under-tension)
- Dead bug press-out to 90/90 heel taps: 3 x 6–8 total alternating reps. Slow 3-second lower on the heel.
- Side plank (knees) longer holds: 2–3 x 20–25 seconds/side.
- Quadruped hover (bear) holds: 3 x 10–15 seconds. Knees 1 inch off floor, spine neutral, steady exhales.
- Suitcase carry (moderate): 2–3 x 30–40 seconds/side.

Week 3 (unilateral/offset emphasis)
- Dead bug with alternating DB press (single DB): 3 x 6–8/side. Resist trunk rotation and flexion as the loaded arm changes.
- Side plank (staggered knees or short-lever feet): 2 x 20–25 seconds/side. Option: add top-arm reach to ceiling to stack ribs/pelvis.
- Half-kneeling anti-rotation press to overhead raise: 2–3 x 6–8/side. Press band out, then raise to forehead height without spine movement.
- Front rack carry (single DB): 2 x 25–35 seconds/side. Elbow slightly forward, ribs down.

Week 4 (density and complexity, still low impact)
- Dead bug with banded pulldown (anti-extension + anti-flexion): 3 x 6–8/side. Band anchored overhead; pull down as heel taps on exhale.
- Side plank (feet, short lever) or long-lever knees: 2–3 x 20–30 seconds/side. Quality over duration.
- Bear hover shoulder taps (slow): 2–3 x 6–8/side. Minimal pelvis shift.
- Suitcase carry or front rack carry (slightly heavier): 2–3 x 35–45 seconds/side.

Optional micro-practice (5–7 minutes on off days)
- 3D rib breathing x 5 breaths
- Dead bug variation of the week x 1 set
- Side plank hold x 1 set/side
- 1 carry x 1 bout/side

Coaching cues and regressions
- Brace: “Exhale, zip up from pelvic floor, ribs soften, then move.”
- Neutral: Keep ribs stacked over pelvis; avoid tucking so hard you lose breath or clench.
- If coning/heaviness: Shorten lever (bend knees/arms closer), decrease range, add more support (incline for bear taps, tall-kneeling instead of standing presses), lighten band/DB, or reduce hold time.
- Progression knobs: Increase hold time by 5–10 seconds, add 1–2 reps, slow eccentrics, or move load farther from midline (longer lever/offset).

Integration notes
- This complements the existing plan’s anti-rotation and anti-extension work while biasing anti-flexion with side planks, bears, dead-bug press-outs, and unilateral carries.
- Pair 2–3 movements per session (one supine + one lateral or quadruped + one carry). Keep total core work ~8–12 minutes to protect recovery.

You can do a simple, repeatable screen in-session to establish a baseline and track change. Focus on function (tension/transfer) more than finger-gap size. Reassess every 1–2 weeks and when you progress load or complexity.

What to look for
- Visible coning/doming along the midline during effort
- Ability to generate tension in the linea alba (feels like a trampoline vs. a soft sinkhole)
- Symptom response: pelvic pressure/heaviness, back pain, or breath-holding to complete reps
- Coordination: can she exhale-to-exert and maintain ribcage over pelvis without excessive bearing down?

Quick self-palpation screen (supine)
- Position: Supine, knees bent, feet on floor. One hand behind head for support.
- Landmarks: Use your other hand to palpate midline at three sites: above the navel (2–3 cm), at the navel, and below the navel (2–3 cm).
- Procedure:
  1) At rest: Note baseline width and depth by gently pressing fingertip pads vertically into the linea alba.
  2) Head lift: Ask her to exhale gently, then lift head/shoulders just enough to clear the floor. Feel for:
     - Width: how many finger widths between the rectus bellies (record per site).
     - Depth/tension: how the tissue responds under your fingers. “Good” is springy/tensioned; “poor” is fingers sinking deeply with little resistance.
  3) Breath and brace: Repeat the head lift after cueing a soft pelvic floor lift and 360° exhale-to-exert. Does tension improve? Does doming reduce?
  4) Progression challenge: If tolerated, test during an easier exertion: heel tap, bridge, or supported sit-to-stand. Watch for coning and feel if tension holds.
- Record: Date, site (above/at/below), width (fingers), depth (shallow/moderate/deep), tension quality (firm/springy vs. soft), and symptom notes.

Standing/functional screen
- Posture and breath: In standing, can she inhale laterally and posteriorly without rib flare or belly push? Stacked ribs over pelvis?
- During movements: Observe midline during:
  - Sit-to-stand, counter-height push-up, loaded carry, RDL hinge pattern
  - Any supine core drill you program (dead bug, heel taps)
- Criteria: No uncontrolled coning or breath-holding; she can maintain tension with exhale on effort.

Interpreting findings
- A gap alone is not a fail. Many women have 2–3 finger widths that function well. Prioritize:
  - Can she create tension and transfer load without symptoms?
  - Does tension improve with cueing? If yes, keep training within that “good tension” zone.
  - If width decreases but depth stays “soft,” stay with regressions until tension improves.
- Red flags for referral to pelvic health PT:
  - Persistent doming you can’t modify with breath/position/load
  - Pain, bulge/pressure, incontinence, or feelings of instability
  - No improvement in tension over 4–6 weeks despite coaching

How to modify based on screen
- If doming or soft sink persists:
  - Regress lever length (bend knees, shorter reach), reduce load, or increase external support (incline push-ups, supported rows).
  - Emphasize exhale-to-exert and slower eccentrics; cue “zip ribs to pelvis” without over-bracing.
  - Use positions that facilitate tension: side-lying, tall-/half-kneeling, heels-elevated bridges.
- If tension good and symptom-free:
  - Progress one variable at a time: load, lever, tempo, or complexity (unilateral/anti-rotation).
  - Recheck after the new stimulus and 24 hours later.

Suggested tracking sheet (per reassessment)
- Resting width (above/at/below umbilicus)
- Depth/tension quality (springy/moderate/soft)
- Movement tested (e.g., head lift, heel tap, counter push-up)
- Coning Y/N; symptoms Y/N
- Notes on cues that improved tension (exhale, hand support, position)
- Decision: progress/maintain/regress; next check date

Education points for the client
- Explain that diastasis is common and can function well with good tension and coordination.
- Progress is non-linear; aim for better control and symptom-free activity rather than a specific “gap” number.
- Encourage reporting of any new heaviness, doming, or leakage during daily tasks.

Great that she’s feeling good. You can nudge intensity, but make small, test–retest changes and keep the postpartum guardrails: progress one variable at a time, stay symptom-free during and 24 hours after, and avoid jumping until cleared.

How to turn the dial safely (mid-Week 2 onward)
- Raise RPE slightly: From 6–7 to 6.5–7.5 on working sets.
- Add only one: load, volume, range, or density—not all at once. Reassess diastasis tension and pelvic floor symptoms after the session and next day.

Strength adjustments
- Load: Increase DB weight 5–10% where form is rock solid (goblet squat, RDL, rows, floor press). If DBs are fixed and light, slow eccentrics to 3–4 seconds or add a 1–2 second pause in the hardest position (e.g., bottom of squat).
- Volume: Add 1–2 reps per set (keeping 1–2 reps in reserve) or add a 4th round to one circuit per session.
- Density: Trim rest by ~10–15 seconds between sets on one lift, not all.
- Range: Remove the box on squats if control/tension holds; deepen split-squat range with support.
- Unilateral/offset: Introduce one unilateral progression earlier from Week 3:
  - Kickstand RDL instead of bilateral RDL (8–10/side, 2–3-sec eccentric).
  - Offset goblet hold for squats (single DB slightly off-center, switch sides each set).
  - Front-rack or heavier suitcase carry 35–45 seconds/side.

Core intensification (anti-flexion focus without crunches)
- Progress side planks: Extend hold to 20–25 seconds or move from knees to short-lever feet.
- Bear hovers: Add 2–3 seconds to holds or slow shoulder taps 2 x 6/side if no coning.
- Dead-bug variations: Add banded pulldown or DB press-out as she heel-taps (6–8/side).
- Carries: Increase duration by 5–10 seconds or load slightly; maintain upright posture.

Cardio dial-up (still no impact)
- Spin sessions: Keep seated. Shift intervals a week earlier if symptom-free.
  - Example mid-Week-2 tweak: 6 x 60 seconds at RPE ~7, 90 seconds easy, then 5–10 minutes steady Zone 2.
- Session length: Add 3–5 minutes to one cardio session (cap ~35 minutes).
- Density finisher: Low-impact circuit 8–12 minutes at RPE 6.5–7 (farmer carry, good mornings, step-ups, marching bridge).

Decision checkpoints each session
- During: No pain >3/10, no visible coning you can’t fix with breath/position, no pelvic heaviness or leakage, no compensatory breath-holding.
- After/next day: No delayed heaviness/pressure, unusual back/pelvic pain, or spike in fatigue that bleeds into daily function.

If any symptom shows up
- Immediately back off the newest progression (load/lever/density), return to the prior successful variation, and retest next session.
- Consider swapping one higher-pressure move for a more supported version that day (e.g., floor press instead of lower incline push-up; bilateral RDL instead of kickstand).

Example “pushed” sessions (starting next workout)
- Strength A (Week 2, adjusted)
  - Keep 3 rounds; add a 4th optional if RPE ≤7.5 and symptom-free.
  - Goblet squat to box: 10 reps with 3-sec eccentric
  - DB RDL pair: 10 reps with 3–4-sec eccentric
  - Incline push-up: 10 reps; lower the surface slightly if clean
  - Half-kneeling 1-arm row: 10–12/side
  - Suitcase carry: 40 seconds/side, moderate load
  - Core add-on: Side plank (knees) 2 x 20–25 sec/side

- Spin (Week 2, adjusted)
  - 5 min easy
  - 6 x 60 s at RPE 7, 90 s easy (all seated)
  - 5–8 min steady RPE 5–6
  - 3–5 min cool-down

Short answer: yes, but keep it low-impact, symptom-screened, and dose-controlled. We’ll use cycling-based HIIT and mixed low-impact intervals. No jumping, no all-out sprints, stay seated on the bike for “hard” efforts. Start with 1 HIIT day/week in Week 2, move to 2 days/week by Week 4 if symptom-free. Pair with strength or on separate days.

Guardrails
- Intensity cap: Hard intervals RPE 7–8/10 (not max). Easy recoveries RPE 3–4.
- Work:rest: Start 1:2–1:3. Minimum 48 hours between HIIT days. Total HIIT volume ≤20 minutes of work/week initially.
- Stop/modify if you see pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, doming, back/pelvic pain, or breath-holding.
- Modalities: Spin bike (preferred), elliptical, low-step step-ups, loaded carries circuits. No running/jumping this block.

Weekly placement
- Option A (paired with strength): Do strength first, then a shortened HIIT finisher (8–12 minutes). Keep total session ≤60 minutes.
- Option B (standalone): Alternate days with strength. Example: Mon Strength, Tue HIIT, Thu Strength, Sat HIIT or steady cardio.

HIIT menu (choose 1 per HIIT day)

Bike HIIT (seated only)
- Intro (Week 2): 6–8 x 30 seconds hard (RPE 7–8), 90 seconds easy. 5-min warm-up, 5-min cool-down. Total 20–24 minutes.
- Build (Week 3): 8–10 x 45 seconds hard, 90 seconds easy. Stay seated; moderate resistance that lets you hold 80–95 rpm without grinding.
- Peak (Week 4): 6–8 x 60 seconds hard, 90 seconds easy. If symptom-free, last 2 reps at RPE 8. Remain seated.

Elliptical HIIT (low impact)
- Week 2: 8 x 40 seconds hard, 80 seconds easy.
- Week 3: 10 x 40 seconds hard, 80 seconds easy.
- Week 4: 8 x 60 seconds hard, 90 seconds easy.

Low-impact mixed modal HIIT (circuit; no jumping)
Format: 30–40 seconds work, 60–90 seconds easy walk or rest between stations. 2–4 rounds, 8–12 total hard intervals.
- Station ideas:
  - Farmer carry brisk walk (light–moderate DBs)
  - Low step-ups with controlled knee drive (alternate legs each interval)
  - Bodyweight good mornings or band-resisted hip hinge
  - Incline mountain climber (hands on counter/bench) at steady cadence
  - Seated or standing band row “sprints” (fast pulls, ribs down)
Keep cadence snappy but controlled; breathe out on effort.

How to progress across Weeks 2–4
- Week 2: 1 HIIT session. Choose Bike Intro or Mixed HIIT with 8–10 total hard intervals (≤12 min hard work).
- Week 3: 1–2 HIIT sessions, alternate modalities if desired. Keep total hard work ≤16 minutes/week.
- Week 4: 2 HIIT sessions if symptom-free. Cap any single session’s hard work at 10–12 minutes.

Pairing with the on-ramp plan (example)
- Mon: Strength A + optional 8-minute Mixed HIIT finisher (4 x 40s hard/80s easy farmer carry + step-ups)
- Wed: Bike HIIT (Week progression above)
- Thu: Strength B
- Sat: Steady spin 25–35 minutes (or Elliptical) OR, in Week 4, a second HIIT session

Coaching cues
- Seat height/handlebars slightly higher to reduce trunk flexion; stay seated during hard bouts.
- RPE check each interval at 20 seconds: if breath is chaotic or she’s bracing/bearing down, back off resistance or cadence.
- Between intervals: nasal or nose-in/mouth-out breathing to downshift.

Recovery and nutrition
- Minimum 24–48 hours between HIIT; keep steps and gentle mobility on “off” days.
- Hydration 2–3 L/day; small carb/protein snack pre (e.g., yogurt + fruit) and 20–30 g protein within 1–2 hours post-session.
- Sleep: Trade volume for sleep—if nights are rough, reduce intervals that day.

When to pause HIIT and refer
- Any persistent pelvic symptoms, unresolving coning, bleeding increase, or pain >3/10. If issues recur despite scaling, refer to a pelvic health PT.

Short answer: plan a graded return-to-run screen and build starting after impact is cleared and she passes key strength/plyometric checks. With her timeline (10–13 weeks postpartum now, no jumping until ~14 weeks), most do best beginning a return-to-run prep phase around 12–16+ weeks postpartum, then ease into run/walk intervals. A 10K in autumn is realistic if you progress methodically and stay symptom-free.

Prerequisites before first run
- Medical: OB/midwife clearance for impact.
- Symptom-free baseline: No pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, pain, or unmanageable abdominal doming in daily life, walking, or strength work; no increase in vaginal bleeding.
- Strength/control (both sides):
  - Sit-to-stand from a standard chair x 10 without compensation.
  - Single-leg calf raises x 20.
  - Side plank (knees or short lever feet) x 30 seconds/side without dipping.
  - Single-leg balance x 30 seconds eyes open.
  - Split squat x 10/side, controlled, pain-free.
  - Hop readiness (introduced only after clearance): pogo holds 3 x 20 seconds, low step “snap downs” x 10/side without symptoms.
- Walking base: Comfortable 30–40 minutes brisk walk without symptoms or next-day heaviness.

Return-to-run screening (first session after impact clearance)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes brisk walk + dynamic mobility.
- Impact readiness checks:
  - March in place x 60 seconds
  - Low-amplitude jog-in-place x 60 seconds
  - Single-leg pogo hold 3 x 10–15 seconds/side (isometric; no bouncing)
  - Step-off landings from 10–15 cm step x 8/side
Observe for pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, pain, or visible doming. If any appear, regress and continue low-impact prep 1–2 more weeks.

Initial run/walk progression (2–3 days/week, 48 hours between)
- Week 0 (first impact week): Run/walk 1:2 x 8–10 reps (e.g., 1 minute easy jog, 2 minutes walk), total 24–30 minutes. Flat, soft surface if possible. RPE 5–6.
- Week 1: 2:2 x 6–8 reps (24–32 minutes).
- Week 2: 3:2 x 5–6 reps (25–30 minutes).
- Week 3: 4:1 x 5 reps (25 minutes).
- Week 4: Continuous easy run 20–25 minutes if symptom-free; otherwise hold at a successful interval week and add minutes gradually.
Rules
- Progress only if symptom-free during and for 24 hours after. If symptoms arise, stop, walk, and in the next session drop back one step (shorter run intervals, longer walks, flatter surface) or pause a week.
- Keep stride compact, cadence a bit higher (165–180) to reduce vertical oscillation; breathe easy and avoid breath-holding/bearing down.

Strength to support running (2x/week alongside)
- Hinge: RDL or hip thrust 3 x 8–10
- Squat or split squat 3 x 8–10/side
- Calf/soleus: Straight-leg and bent-knee calf raises 3 x 12–15/side
- Single-leg stability: Step-downs or lateral step-downs 2–3 x 6–8/side
- Core/resist rotation: Side plank, Pallof press, carries 2–3 x 20–30 seconds
- Plyo prep (after impact clearance, symptom-free): Pogo holds, ankle hops in place, low step hops, progressing amplitude over 4–6 weeks

10K timeline planning (example if cleared for impact at ~14 weeks postpartum)
- Weeks 14–18 pp: Run/walk build to continuous 25–30 minutes easy.
- Weeks 18–22 pp: Extend long run to 35–45 minutes; add one short interval day (e.g., 6 x 1 minute steady with 2 minutes easy).
- Weeks 22–26 pp: Two to three runs/week. One longer easy run (45–55 minutes), one easy recovery (20–30 minutes), one quality session (tempos or short intervals) if fully symptom-free.
- Final 4–6 weeks before the race: Specific 10K prep. Long run 60–70 minutes max easy; introduce controlled 10K-pace intervals such as 4–6 x 5 minutes at RPE 7 with 2–3 minutes easy. Keep one strength day; drop or scale if fatigue or pelvic symptoms emerge.

Red flags and when to pause/refer
- Pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, visible doming you can’t resolve with breath or posture, sharp pelvic/back pain, or bleeding increase during or after runs.
- If symptoms persist despite reducing volume/intensity and improving mechanics, refer to a pelvic health physical therapist.

Practical cues
- Posture: Tall, ribs over pelvis, slight forward lean from ankles.
- Foot strike: Quiet, under center of mass; avoid overstriding.
- Cadence: Aim for quick feet, compact steps.
- Recovery: Add an easy day or cross-train after any run that produces unusual fatigue; prioritize sleep and fueling.

With steady, symptom-led progress, she can be comfortably running 3 days/week by mid-summer and sharpen for a fall 10K safely.

Here’s a concise, week-by-week summary of the 4-week on-ramp (10–13 weeks postpartum), including strength, cardio/HIIT add-ons, core focus, and what to screen for as you progress.

Week 1 (acclimatisation)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 2 rounds each, RPE ~5–6. Patterns: sit-to-box squats, DB RDL drills, incline push-ups (wall/counter), half-/tall-kneeling rows/pulldowns, glute bridges, supported split-squat taps, light carries.
- Core (anti-flexion add-on): Dead-bug ISO press 2 x 5–6/side; side plank (knees) 2 x 12–15s/side; tall-kneeling anti-extension pulldown 2 x 8–10; suitcase carry 2 x 20–30s/side.
- Cardio: 2–3 easy walks (20–30 min). Optional spin 15–20 min steady (RPE 5–6).
- HIIT: None yet.
- Screen/monitor: Baseline diastasis palpation (above/at/below navel), look for doming; symptom log (heaviness, leakage, pain, bleeding changes), breathing/bracing coordination, push-up height tolerance, carry duration.

Week 2 (build volume; option to nudge intensity midweek if symptom-free)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 3 rounds each, RPE ~6–7. Add slow eccentrics and light load: goblet squat to box, DB RDLs, counter push-ups, half-kneeling press/rows, split-squat (supported). Core accessories: side planks, heel slides.
- Core (anti-flexion): Dead-bug press-outs 3 x 6–8; side plank (knees) 2–3 x 20–25s; bear hovers 3 x 10–15s; suitcase carry 2–3 x 30–40s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 25–30 min with 3–4 x 2 min at RPE 6–7 (all seated) or steady walk 25–35 min.
- HIIT: Introduce 1 HIIT session if symptom-free. Example Bike HIIT: 6–8 x 30s hard (RPE 7–8) / 90s easy, seated only. Total hard ≤12 min.
- Screen/monitor: Recheck diastasis tension with head lift and during heel taps/push-ups; watch for new pelvic symptoms during and 24 hours after harder sessions. If great by midweek, you may add 1–2 reps or a 3–4 sec eccentric, or introduce a unilateral progression (kickstand RDL or offset goblet).

Week 3 (add complexity; unilateral/anti-rotation)
- Strength: 3 sessions, ~3 rounds each, RPE ~6–7. Progress to offset goblet squats, kickstand RDLs, lower-incline push-ups, half-kneeling presses, side planks (longer holds), anti-rotation presses, front/suitcase carries.
- Core (anti-flexion): Alternating DB-press dead bug 3 x 6–8/side; side plank (short-lever feet or longer knees) 2 x 20–25s; half-kneeling anti-rotation press-to-overhead 2–3 x 6–8/side; front-rack carry 2 x 25–35s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 28–35 min with 6–8 x 60s at RPE ~7 (seated) or steady walk/elliptical.
- HIIT: 1–2 sessions if symptom-free. Examples: Bike 8–10 x 45s hard / 90s easy, or low-impact mixed circuits (farmer carry, low step-ups, good mornings) 30–40s work / 60–90s easy. Keep total weekly hard ≤16 min.
- Screen/monitor: Functional checks during split squats, push-ups, and carries for coning or breath-holding. Palpate linea alba response if loads/angles change. Confirm no next-day heaviness or leakage as density increases.

Week 4 (pre-transition; density up, still no jumping)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 3–4 rounds, RPE ~6.5–7.5. Goblet squats (no box if clean), kickstand RDLs, lowest-manageable incline push-ups, 1-arm rows, split squats, pulldowns. Shorter rests or small load bumps if symptom-free.
- Core (anti-flexion): Dead bug with banded pulldown 3 x 6–8/side; side plank 2–3 x 20–30s/side; bear shoulder taps 2–3 x 6–8/side; heavier/longer carries 35–45s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 30–40 min with pyramid or 3 x 4 min at RPE ~6.5–7 (seated).
- HIIT: Up to 2 sessions if symptom-free. Example Bike: 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy (seated). Cap per-session hard at 10–12 min; keep 48 hours between HIIT days.
- Screen/monitor: End-of-block reassessment—diastasis tension (supine head lift and under load), symptom log, push-up height change, split-squat depth, carry duration/quality. If all green and OB clears impact after this week, plan return-to-run screening next block.

Always screen for and modify if you observe
- Pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, increasing bleeding, visible midline coning/doming that doesn’t resolve with exhale/position, pain >3/10, or breath-holding/straining. If present, reduce load/lever/density, increase external support (inclines, shorter ranges), and consider pelvic health PT referral if persistent.

Key coaching anchors
- Exhale on effort, soft 360-degree brace with pelvic floor lift; relax on inhale.
- Technique over volume; progress one variable at a time.
- Keep sessions symptom-free during and for 24 hours after.

Here’s a concise, week-by-week summary of the 4-week on-ramp (10–13 weeks postpartum), including strength, cardio/HIIT add-ons, core focus, and what to screen for as you progress.

Week 1 (acclimatisation)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 2 rounds each, RPE ~5–6. Patterns: sit-to-box squats, DB RDL drills, incline push-ups (wall/counter), half-/tall-kneeling rows/pulldowns, glute bridges, supported split-squat taps, light carries.
- Core (anti-flexion add-on): Dead-bug ISO press 2 x 5–6/side; side plank (knees) 2 x 12–15s/side; tall-kneeling anti-extension pulldown 2 x 8–10; suitcase carry 2 x 20–30s/side.
- Cardio: 2–3 easy walks (20–30 min). Optional spin 15–20 min steady (RPE 5–6).
- HIIT: None yet.
- Screen/monitor: Baseline diastasis palpation (above/at/below navel), look for doming; symptom log (heaviness, leakage, pain, bleeding changes), breathing/bracing coordination, push-up height tolerance, carry duration.

Week 2 (build volume; option to nudge intensity midweek if symptom-free)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 3 rounds each, RPE ~6–7. Add slow eccentrics and light load: goblet squat to box, DB RDLs, counter push-ups, half-kneeling press/rows, split-squat (supported). Core accessories: side planks, heel slides.
- Core (anti-flexion): Dead-bug press-outs 3 x 6–8; side plank (knees) 2–3 x 20–25s; bear hovers 3 x 10–15s; suitcase carry 2–3 x 30–40s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 25–30 min with 3–4 x 2 min at RPE 6–7 (all seated) or steady walk 25–35 min.
- HIIT: Introduce 1 HIIT session if symptom-free. Example Bike HIIT: 6–8 x 30s hard (RPE 7–8) / 90s easy, seated only. Total hard ≤12 min.
- Screen/monitor: Recheck diastasis tension with head lift and during heel taps/push-ups; watch for new pelvic symptoms during and 24 hours after harder sessions. If great by midweek, you may add 1–2 reps or a 3–4 sec eccentric, or introduce a unilateral progression (kickstand RDL or offset goblet).

Week 3 (add complexity; unilateral/anti-rotation)
- Strength: 3 sessions, ~3 rounds each, RPE ~6–7. Progress to offset goblet squats, kickstand RDLs, lower-incline push-ups, half-kneeling presses, side planks (longer holds), anti-rotation presses, front/suitcase carries.
- Core (anti-flexion): Alternating DB-press dead bug 3 x 6–8/side; side plank (short-lever feet or longer knees) 2 x 20–25s; half-kneeling anti-rotation press-to-overhead 2–3 x 6–8/side; front-rack carry 2 x 25–35s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 28–35 min with 6–8 x 60s at RPE ~7 (seated) or steady walk/elliptical.
- HIIT: 1–2 sessions if symptom-free. Examples: Bike 8–10 x 45s hard / 90s easy, or low-impact mixed circuits (farmer carry, low step-ups, good mornings) 30–40s work / 60–90s easy. Keep total weekly hard ≤16 min.
- Screen/monitor: Functional checks during split squats, push-ups, and carries for coning or breath-holding. Palpate linea alba response if loads/angles change. Confirm no next-day heaviness or leakage as density increases.

Week 4 (pre-transition; density up, still no jumping)
- Strength: 3 sessions, 3–4 rounds, RPE ~6.5–7.5. Goblet squats (no box if clean), kickstand RDLs, lowest-manageable incline push-ups, 1-arm rows, split squats, pulldowns. Shorter rests or small load bumps if symptom-free.
- Core (anti-flexion): Dead bug with banded pulldown 3 x 6–8/side; side plank 2–3 x 20–30s/side; bear shoulder taps 2–3 x 6–8/side; heavier/longer carries 35–45s/side.
- Cardio: Spin 30–40 min with pyramid or 3 x 4 min at RPE ~6.5–7 (seated).
- HIIT: Up to 2 sessions if symptom-free. Example Bike: 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy (seated). Cap per-session hard at 10–12 min; keep 48 hours between HIIT days.
- Screen/monitor: End-of-block reassessment—diastasis tension (supine head lift and under load), symptom log, push-up height change, split-squat depth, carry duration/quality. If all green and OB clears impact after this week, plan return-to-run screening next block.

Always screen for and modify if you observe
- Pelvic heaviness/pressure, leakage, increasing bleeding, visible midline coning/doming that doesn’t resolve with exhale/position, pain >3/10, or breath-holding/straining. If present, reduce load/lever/density, increase external support (inclines, shorter ranges), and consider pelvic health PT referral if persistent.

Key coaching anchors
- Exhale on effort, soft 360-degree brace with pelvic floor lift; relax on inhale.
- Technique over volume; progress one variable at a time.
- Keep sessions symptom-free during and for 24 hours after.
